0.label: crowned_figure_with_two_staffs_looped_legs
0.description: The pasted print: a thin figure with a tall ridged crown and a stern face, holding an upright staff with a square head in each hand; a ribbed, egg-shaped torso and a belt; legs bent sharply outward and up into a W that meets the staffs.
0.iconography: A crowned ruler with two staffs of office and looped, 'mudfish' legs — the king type shared with EBA-Div_00311_01 and 00312_01. The tall ridged crown recalls the beaded crowns (adé) of the Ado-Ekiti door.

panel.title: Mount sheet: a crowned figure with two staffs and looped legs, from the Modakeke temple board
panel.object_type: archive mount sheet with a printed detail (after Frobenius 1923, pl. 184)
panel.summary: A small print, 'enlarged 2×', of a crowned figure holding two staffs, captioned 'from Plate 184 … partial drawing of a carved temple board, excavated by the D.I.A.F.E. in 1910 at Modeke [Modakeke], Yorubaland'.

register_readings.reading: One figure: tall crown, two staffs, looped legs.

panel.composition: A frontal figure whose staffs and legs make a closed frame around the body.
panel.narrative: The clearest drawing of the collection's king figure: crown, two staffs, legs turned into loops. The same type stands in the middle of the three crowned figures on the Ife planks (EBA-Div_00311_01, 00312_01), so the image travelled between Ife and Modakeke — the two rival towns shared one picture of kingship.
panel.hypotheses: Supports 'chronicle of rulers': a repeated, recognisable king image across towns.
uncertainties: The looped legs could also be a stool or a stylised garment.
